tools_helpful.evidence: session-log.txt lines ~206-210: copied the UWP source (.xaml/.cs/.resw/.appxmanifest/assets) into the target and preserved the UWP .csproj under .uwp-source/, giving the agent a clean starting tree.

tools_problematic.problem: Its manifest checks only cover image-reference resolution + Windows.Desktop/rescap/runFullTrust packaging shape. It does NOT verify that UWP <Extension> declarations the migrated code still depends on (windows.backgroundTasks in particular) were carried into the build Package.appxmanifest, so it passed a manifest that silently breaks Register() at runtime.
tools_problematic.evidence: Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 section 5/5b (lines 277-374) has no <Extension>/backgroundTasks check; the migrated app scored 50 (6x partial) purely from a missing manifest extension.

tool_limitations.limitation: No cross-check between retained UWP background-task code (Windows.ApplicationModel.Background.BackgroundTaskBuilder + string TaskEntryPoint + Register()) and the presence of a matching <Extension Category="windows.backgroundTasks"> in the build manifest.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Add a check: if target *.cs uses the classic BackgroundTaskBuilder/TaskEntryPoint model, FAIL when Package.appxmanifest has no windows.backgroundTasks extension.

failed_apis.why_tried: Sample keeps the classic out-of-process background-task model; RegisterBackgroundTask handler calls builder.Register().
failed_apis.root_cause: The build Package.appxmanifest (app/BackgroundTask/Package.appxmanifest) declares no <Extension Category="windows.backgroundTasks" EntryPoint="Tasks.SampleBackgroundTask">, so Register() throws at runtime (the out-of-process task entry point is not declared).
failed_apis.fix: Merge the UWP manifest's <Extensions>/<Extension Category="windows.backgroundTasks"> declaration(s) into the WinUI 3 build Package.appxmanifest for every retained TaskEntryPoint.

special_apis.special_handling: When the classic model is retained (not ported to WinAppSDK BackgroundTaskBuilder), the app is packaged and the <Extension Category="windows.backgroundTasks"> declaration is a runtime prerequisite of Register(); it must be present in the build manifest with the same EntryPoint string used in code.

errors_encountered.error: Register button dead in all 6 scenarios: Status stays 'Unregistered', Unregister stays disabled, no exception surfaced.
errors_encountered.root_cause: builder.Register() throws because the build manifest lacks the windows.backgroundTasks extension; the click handler has no try/catch, so the exception is swallowed and UpdateUI() is never reached with registered=true.
errors_encountered.fix: (1) Add the windows.backgroundTasks <Extension> to the build manifest; (2) wrap Register() in try/catch and surface the failure in the UI Status text so a missing-declaration failure is never silent.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Agent copied the UWP source manifest into a nested folder (BackgroundTask/BackgroundTask/Package.appxmanifest, which DID contain the two windows.backgroundTasks extensions) but never merged those <Extension> elements into the actual WinUI 3 build manifest (app/BackgroundTask/Package.appxmanifest).
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: The skill's manifest guidance emphasizes image references + Windows.Desktop/rescap/runFullTrust packaging shape; carrying over UWP <Extensions> is only a buried parenthetical, and background tasks specifically are not called out as needing a manifest declaration.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: A Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 check that FAILs when retained background-task code has no matching manifest extension, plus an explicit 'carry over <Extensions>' step in the manifest checklist and the Background Tasks pattern.

missing_tooling.need: Automated detection of UWP manifest <Extension> declarations that the migrated code still depends on but that are missing from the build manifest.
missing_tooling.would_have_saved: All 6 scenarios (the entire behavioral score) — a single FAIL would have flagged the dead Register control before scoring.
